clue.text: One inside skimmed account book, increasingly irritable

indicators.note: inside says the one goes into the middle of the trimmed book
skimmed means the top has been taken off, as cream is skimmed from milk

parts.note: a ledger is a book of accounts
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone poring over a ledger grows more and more tetchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skimmed' takes the top letter off LEDGER to leave EDGER; 'inside' puts I within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means nervous and irritable, and the comparative form means more so.

clue.text: Mark coaches, with son having priority

indicators.note: having priority means going first, so the son's letter jumps to the front

parts.note: coaches are vehicles, cars of a train

explanation.surface: A sports coach's son gets favourable treatment and it leaves a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Coaches are railway carriages, CARS; the S at the end moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark left on the skin by a healed wound.

clue.text: William, third in sports day, is puffed out

parts.note: Bill is the familiar short form of the name William

indicators.note: third in tells us to take the third letter of the word sports

parts.note: Wed is the short form of Wednesday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: A boy called William is out of breath on school sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: Billowed describes sails or clothing swelling outward as air fills them, i.e. puffed out.

clue.text: American lodger's gossip heard

indicators.note: heard says the word for gossip is spoken and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: a rumour is a piece of gossip

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle about a lodger from the United States gets overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: In US English a roomer is someone renting a room in another's house, a lodger.

clue.text: Principally unfaithful husband repeated denial

indicators.note: repeated means the two-letter pair is written out twice
principally means taking the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cheating husband keeps saying it wasn't him.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-uh is an informal spoken no, an expression of refusal or denial.

clue.text: During party in Wales, note semi-cropped style of hair

definitions.note: an adjective describing hair worn in braids, rather than a noun

indicators.note: during says the trimmed note sits within the party's name

parts.note: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party, often just Plaid

indicators.note: semi-cropped means half the word note has been cut away, leaving its second half

explanation.surface: At a Welsh party someone remarks on a half-shorn hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaid Cymru, the Welsh nationalist party, is commonly called just Plaid. 'semi-cropped' keeps only the second half of the word note.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaited hair is braided, woven into strands, a familiar style for wearing it.

clue.text: Old sports presenter sounding ill? TV channel's getting one to stand in

indicators.note: sounding says we write a word pronounced like the slang for unwell

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or unsound, as in a dicky heart

indicators.note: to stand in says the one is placed inside the channel's name

parts.note: Dave is a British TV channel; with the possessive it gives DAVES
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A former sports broadcaster sounds unwell, so the channel finds someone to deputise.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickie Davies fronted ITV's World of Sport for years. DICKY is British slang for poorly; Dave is a UK TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickie Davies was a long-serving British television sports presenter, best known for World of Sport.

clue.text: Entertainer with bird having a port at the bar

indicators.note: at says the port sits right beside the bar, after it

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
Hull is a port city in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A performer with a parrot stands drinking at the bar of a port tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Hull was a British entertainer whose act centred on Emu, an unruly bird puppet. Hull is an English port.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Hull was the comedian always seen with Emu, his aggressive bird puppet.

clue.text: Even auntie relocated after visiting hot area of central France

indicators.note: after visiting places the rearranged letters following the hot letter

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: relocated means the letters of even auntie are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An aunt moves house after a trip somewhere hot in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Haute-Vienne is a French department in the Limousin region, around Limoges.

clue.text: Institute rules, and calm unconfined area of N. England

parts.note: the WI is the Women's Institute
R abbreviates rule; doubled it stands for the plural, as pp does for pages

indicators.note: unconfined means the outer letters of calm are let go, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A local institute's regulations promote quiet in a northern district.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wirral is a peninsula in Merseyside and Cheshire, in north-west England.

clue.text: Furniture branch the head of company locks

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a river or organisation

indicators.note: the head of means just the first letter of company

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A branch manager admires the company boss's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a padded seat with side supports, a common item of furniture.

clue.text: When racing, GB rider entertains wife at West Country town

indicators.note: entertains says the rearranged rider letters hold the wife and at
racing means the letters of GB rider are set in rapid motion and jumbled

explanation.surface: A British jockey hosts his wife while competing at a racecourse town.
explanation.walkthrough: GB looks like a nationality label for the rider, but its letters join the anagram. Bridgwater is in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridgwater is a market town in Somerset, part of England's West Country.

clue.text: Brace secures centre of Rome cathedral

indicators.note: secures means holding the middle letters fast inside

parts.note: a brace is a pair, a duo

indicators.note: centre of picks the two middle letters of Rome

explanation.surface: A support bracket holds up the middle of a Roman cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Duomo is the Italian word for a city's principal church, as in Florence's famous one.

clue.text: Ex-England bowler unleashed heartless flyer towards tot, retreating

indicators.note: towards says the bird is followed by the next piece, heading to it
heartless takes out the middle letter

parts.note: unleashed means set free
a tit is a small bird, a flyer

indicators.note: retreating means the word for tot goes backwards

parts.note: to tot up is to sum

explanation.surface: A cruel bird is released and flies at a toddler, who backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Titmus was a Middlesex and England off-spin bowler. Tot as a verb means add up, SUM, which 'retreating' turns to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Titmus played Test cricket for England as a spin bowler from the 1950s to the 1970s.

clue.text: Short female sprinter's defeat, exhausting run, absorbs judge

indicators.note: absorbs says the trimmed word takes the judge inside
exhausting means using up, so the run is taken away

parts.note: to floor someone is to defeat them
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sprinter loses, worn out by her run, and takes in what the judge says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' signals a nickname: Flo-Jo was Florence Griffith Joyner.
explanation.definitionFit: Flo-Jo was the nickname of Florence Griffith Joyner, the American Olympic sprint champion.

clue.text: Delight shown by little woman seeing Northern band

parts.note: joy is delight
Di is a short form of the woman's name Diana
vision is the faculty of seeing

explanation.surface: A small woman is thrilled to spot a band from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: Joy Division was a post-punk band from Manchester in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy Division was a Manchester rock group of the late 1970s, fronted by Ian Curtis.

clue.text: What's altered after retired soldiers explored leisurely?

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the soldiers
retired means withdrawn, going back, so the soldiers' letters run backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: altered says the letters of what's are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A question about what changed once the old soldiers had wandered around.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is to tour places of interest at leisure; this is its past tense.

clue.text: Punish boy, audibly drunk

parts.note: boy! and cor! are both British exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: audibly says the slang word for drunk is spoken and we write only what it sounds like

parts.note: wrecked is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A command to discipline a lad who is clearly intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'boy!'. The silent W and the voiced D drop out when WRECKED is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a child is to discipline or punish them for misbehaving.

clue.text: I don't like that stifling new rock singer

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, holding the new letter inside

parts.note: boo is the shout of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles while silencing a new rock vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bono is the lead vocalist of the Irish rock group U2.

clue.text: Perhaps kitchen assistant's gone to work around five with relishes

definitions.note: a pair of items that help a cook, defined by example

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round the five
to work means the letters of gone are put to work in a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
to relish something is to love it

explanation.surface: A kitchen helper has left for work at about five, with jars of chutney.
explanation.definitionFit: Padded mitts used for handling hot dishes are a cook's helper, hence the hedged example definition.

clue.text: Measuring device's function discovered in time

indicators.note: discovered in means found inside, so the function sits within the month

parts.note: Oct, October, is a time of year
tan, tangent, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A maths instrument's function is uncovered over time.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is a navigational instrument for measuring angles, forerunner of the sextant.

clue.text: Forcibly remove regulars in Bull and Stag's Head in evening

indicators.note: in says these letters sit inside the word for evening

parts.note: eve is an old word for evening

indicators.note: regulars means taking every second letter of Bull
head means the first letter of Stag's

explanation.surface: Pub regulars at the Bull and the Stag's Head are thrown out one evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bull and the Stag's Head read as pub names, but give UL and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To evulse is to pluck or tear out by force, a rare formal verb.

clue.text: Donald Duck seen in Tennessee for kids' TV programme once

parts.note: Donald Trump, the US president

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for Tennessee
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: Donald Duck makes a cartoon appearance in Tennessee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donald Duck' looks like the cartoon character, but splits into TRUMP and O. Trumpton was a 1960s British children's stop-motion series.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpton was a classic British children's animated series from 1967 about a town's fire brigade.

clue.text: Let me see about drying out dog

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the hesitation reads backwards

parts.note: um is the hesitant noise of someone thinking
TT, teetotal, describes someone off alcohol, drying out

explanation.surface: Someone pondering a dog that is drying off after a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutt is a mongrel, an informal word for a dog of mixed breed.

clue.text: See 14
Clean-cut pair of trunks creator's joining

indicators.note: pair of means the first two letters of trunks

parts.note: the creator is the setter, so creator's is I'm, I am

explanation.surface: The setter joins in, wearing smart swimming trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim means neat and tidy in appearance, as clean-cut does.

clue.text: Beware using current container coated in mercury

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: coated in means wrapped by the mercury symbol on both sides

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: A warning about electrical equipment in a mercury-lined vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Achtung is German for attention, used in English as a warning to look out.

clue.text: See 7
